title: Invalidate composed artwork when its selected inputs change
body: After a preview has rendered, changing the photo, featured attempt, or overlay style starts another asynchronous composition without clearing `composedBlob`, and Publish remains enabled. `handlePublishToFeed` captures that previous blob here and uploads it even if the replacement finishes during reconciliation; the inserted post and source photo use the new selections. This can publish the wrong photograph or outcome with mismatched Feed facts. Bind the cached artifact to its input revision and require the matching preview before publishing.

title: Guard the ended-session reconciliation against account changes
body: If logout or an account switch occurs while the `ended_at` update is in flight, its successful response executes these setters before the identity check at line 765. `setPastSessions` inserts the captured previous user's session, including private notes, into the newly cleared/current journal; `setSessionToPublish` can also stamp a different account's open composer with the old operation's timestamp. Check the initiating identity before this newly added reconciliation block, not only after post insertion.

title: Remove cleanup ownership before reusing committed artwork keys
body: When an insert is confirmed absent but `storage.remove` fails, lines 747–753 retain its keys in `pending_cleanup` while preserving the operation ID. Retrying in the same tab reuses those keys and can successfully create the post, but this success branch clears only the intent and operation ID. The next Log load calls `retryPendingCleanups`, which blindly deletes those now-live images, leaving the public post without artwork. Reconcile queued cleanup ownership when retrying/committing and verify references before deletion.

title: Exclude active publications from recovery cleanup
body: An intent is recorded before either upload, but this branch treats every currently absent post as abandoned. `fetchSessionData` starts recovery whenever its `[user]` dependency changes, and `user-store.ts` replaces that object on token refresh; opening Log in another tab also runs recovery against the same localStorage intents. If recovery runs after the composed upload and before insertion, it deletes that image and clears the recovery record while the original handler continues and commits a post pointing to the deleted key. Distinguish active operations from abandoned recovery work and serialize cleanup with publication.

title: Preserve durable operation identity across publication retries
body: Operation IDs come from tab-scoped sessionStorage, but recovery intents live in localStorage. If a previous upload's status remains unknown and the user retries from a new tab—or after Save Privately clears the operation ID—`getOrCreatePublicationOperationId` allocates a different ID, and this filter silently discards the original intent before reconciling it. The replacement can publish successfully while the previous uncommitted photograph/card remain public with no recoverable keys. Reuse the retained durable operation or reconcile and retain its assets before replacing it.

title: Bound outcome-specific alt text to the database character limit
body: These longer failed-outcome templates can reject publication for inputs that previously fit `session_posts_image_alt_length` (300 characters). A schema-valid 120-character route, 24-character grade, 120-character venue, and 20-character display name produce exactly 300 characters with the old sent template, but 313 for `fell` and 316 for `stopped`; Log inserts this string unchanged after uploading and ending the session. Bound the generated alternative using Unicode-safe character handling while retaining the actual outcome.

title: Keep the catalog link for repeated attempts on the same climb
body: After the first logged attempt this clears the route link even though the route name, grade, and discipline remain selected. A normal second try or eventual send on that same catalog climb is therefore inserted with `route_id: null`; featuring that send loses the route metadata, Beta destination, and bookmark control in Feed. The new name-change handler and explicit Detach control already handle switching to a manual climb, so retain the link until the user actually changes/detaches the selection.

title: Ignore bubbled keys from the history row's action buttons
body: Enter and Space on the nested Publish button bubble to this new row handler, which prevents the native button activation and opens session details instead. Consequently keyboard users cannot activate the history Publish action directly, despite the semantic button. Handle only events originating on the row itself, or rely on the dedicated Details button rather than intercepting its descendants' keyboard events.

title: Scope publication-attempt responses to the selected session
body: This new history fetch checks only the user ID. Open publication for session A, cancel while its attempts are loading, then open session B: if A's request completes last, it overwrites B's `publishAttempts` and featured ID while `sessionToPublish` still points to B. The preview shows A's climb, and insertion fails the database trigger requiring the featured attempt to belong to the posted session. Invalidate pending composer requests on close/target change and accept results only for the current target/generation.

title: Reset in-flight mutation flags when the account changes
body: The new identity guard skips clearing `isStartingSession` when account A's request finishes after logout/account B signs in, but the identity-reset effect never resets that flag. In the still-mounted Log page, Begin Session consequently remains disabled indefinitely for the new user. The same pattern affects `isLoggingAttempt` and `isPublishing`. Reset all identity-scoped pending state when replacing the account while continuing to reject old request data.

title: Retain the intent when persisting cleanup ownership fails
body: `addPendingCleanups` swallows localStorage write/quota errors, yet recovery unconditionally clears the durable intent immediately afterward. If the cleanup record cannot be written and the subsequent storage removal fails, both uploaded public keys are forgotten; the same loss occurs in Log's failed-insert cleanup branch. Only clear the original intent after durable cleanup ownership has actually been persisted or deletion has succeeded.

title: Preserve the unknown session state while retrying its read
body: Retry Connection calls this function, which clears `sessionLoadError` before the active-session query has returned. The main render checks only that error and `activeSession`, not a pending session-status state, so a failed initial lookup followed by Retry immediately exposes an enabled Begin Session form even when a live session already exists. Similarly, retrying failed attempt loading re-enables Log with the incomplete attempt count. Keep mutations gated until the corresponding status/attempt read has succeeded.

title: Provide a browser boundary for the new Node storage tests
body: The repository runs this file with `node --test`, but its setup defines localStorage/sessionStorage without defining `window`. All storage helpers therefore take their `typeof window === 'undefined'` branches: cleanup reads return empty arrays, operation IDs are regenerated, and `recordPublicationIntent` throws before reaching the quota-error test. The newly added storage/recovery tests consequently fail under the configured runner rather than exercising the intended behavior. Supply and restore the browser boundary or use an explicit injectable storage dependency.
